title: V0 combines ask classification, readiness, and release impact
body: These three items form one operator workflow: classify the ask, identify what can run next or in parallel, and catch documentation/release surfaces that need updates before dispatch or merge. Decision queue and UX-aware planning remain future roadmap milestones.

title: Read-only recommender, not scheduler
body: `dontpanic next` must not dispatch or mutate state. It surfaces ready/not-ready reasoning, collision warnings, and candidate commands so an operator or agent can decide what to run.

title: Substrate collision is heuristic in v0
body: Feature steps, allowed_paths, and active supervisor metadata are incomplete proxies for write conflicts. V0 warnings should be conservative and advisory; hard conflict prevention waits for richer touched-files metadata.

title: Root changelog is product-facing
body: `claude/shared/CHANGELOG.md` remains the schema/agent-conventions changelog. Root `CHANGELOG.md` tracks public/product-facing DontPanic changes and links to README/onboarding/architecture/dashboard updates when relevant.

title: Collision warnings prefer precision over recall in v0
body: V0 collision warnings should fire only on strong signals: same plan/feature, or active-supervisor overlap with intersecting allowed_paths/path-like step tokens. False negatives are acceptable in v0; noisy false positives would teach operators to ignore the recommender. If real collisions slip through, a later plan can add richer touched-file metadata and tighten recall.

title: Fleet mode is aggregation, not scheduling
body: `dontpanic next --scope fleet` reads the project registry and runs the repo-scoped analyzer per active project, then aggregates/ranks the results. It does not coordinate cross-project dispatch, normalize every cross-version schema shape, or claim that independent projects share one process. This child plan depends on the dashboard project-selector substrate because fleet semantics require registered project identity.

title: Release-impact substrate is draft intent plus lock-time diff
body: Draft-time release-impact advice uses `surfaces`, `allowed_paths`, and feature step path tokens because no implementation diff exists yet. Lock-time advice may use git diff against the working branch/main when available. `dontpanic next` is the primary output surface; plan-lock messaging is secondary; no v0 evidence sidecar is required.

title: Root changelog path-pattern rule
body: Root `CHANGELOG.md` is required or strongly suggested for README/public docs, getting-started/onboarding/init/doctor behavior, dashboard UX/state shapes, operator-visible CLI commands, capability manifests/setup guidance, and public metadata/social preview/discoverability assets. `claude/shared/CHANGELOG.md` is sufficient for agent-conventions/schema changes that do not alter public DontPanic behavior. Internal runtime changes, tests, evidence, and plan ledger updates usually need no root changelog unless they change a public workflow.

title: Planning intelligence opens now because operator capacity is the bottleneck
body: Several older lanes remain active or blocked (Firebase dashboard adapter, external integrations bridge, OpenClaw umbrella, F006 budget semantics), but the cross-lane bottleneck is the operator manually reconstructing readiness, dependencies, and release/documentation obligations. Shipping this V0 first should make the remaining lanes easier to sequence. Existing lanes stay tracked; this roadmap does not supersede them.

title: Budget and breaker state are readiness inputs when available
body: If the recommender can read known gate, breaker, or budget exhaustion state, it should warn or mark work not-ready when dispatch would likely hit a known pause. If the substrate cannot be read, it should disclose the unknown rather than treating the feature as clean. F006 budget semantics does not gate this plan; v0 consumes existing signals opportunistically.

title: Schema remains unchanged for investigations and design specs
body: F001 introduces guidance vocabulary for investigations and design/product specifications, but does not add schema-level `plan_kind` or typed design/spec plan shapes. First-class schema enforcement remains V3 of the roadmap after repeated roadmap-style usage proves the need.

title: Real-inventory dogfood required
body: Fixture outputs are not sufficient evidence for `dontpanic next`. F002 must save `dontpanic-next-real-inventory-output.json` generated against the current DontPanic active plan inventory so the operator can judge whether recommendations are useful, noisy, or misleading before later decision-queue work builds on the recommender.

title: V0 quality gates V1 decision-queue work
body: V1's decision queue should not be drafted merely because V0 produces friction. If V0 is noisy or wrong, the next step is to fix the recommender, not build a richer queue on top of untrusted readiness output. Observe at least one to two weeks of V0 use before promoting V1 unless a concrete missed-decision incident clearly requires it.

title: F001 accepted after signed-off DontPanic volley
body: F001 ran through DontPanic with Claude implementer and Codex auditor. First run paused at pre_merge after auditor signoff; operator approved pre_merge. Rerun with the unrelated architecture.json dirty state explicitly noted returned terminal status signed_off after one round. signoff_writer skipped because closeout-memo.md was absent, so the operator updated features.json to passes:true using the signed-off implementer/auditor envelopes as evidence. This records the actual DontPanic result without re-dispatching further.

title: F002 closed after manual remediation of stopped run
body: F002 initially stopped with no_progress after the second implementer run timed out and the auditor found missing real-inventory dogfood evidence plus an inconsistent malformed-plan fixture. The operator remediated those findings directly: invalid-frontmatter load-error coverage replaced the no-features fixture, roadmap-parent fallback gained explicit regression coverage, active roadmap parents no longer block their child plans, and `evidence/goal-governance/post_impl/infra/operator-finds-parallel-work-without-reading-every-plan/dontpanic-next-real-inventory-output.json` was generated from the current DontPanic inventory. Targeted F002 tests passed with 22 tests, plan validation passed, and `dontpanic close --operator-resolved ... --reason operator_judgment --allow-missing-breaker` recorded the closeout.

title: F003 accepted after signed-off audit and patch-completeness hygiene
body: F003 ran through DontPanic with Claude implementer and Codex auditor. The first auditor round requested changes; the second auditor round signed off with no findings after verifying the release-impact mapper and advisory surfaces. The supervisor then blocked terminal completion on patch-completeness hygiene (unstaged F003 files and a missing literal `## Return Condition` heading in the existing closeout memo), not on implementation correctness. The operator added the return-condition heading, verified targeted F003+F002 tests with 54 passed, validated the plan schema, and updated F003 evidence_refs/passes:true using the signed-off auditor envelope plus release-impact docs and real-inventory output.
